title: Preserve Montgomery County v. Montgomery County (Judge Lets Sunshine Law Challenge to Amazon Data Center Incentives Proceed)
jurisdiction: Circuit Court of Cole County, Missouri
amount: Not a monetary claim; advocacy group seeks to halt a data center project over alleged Sunshine Law and public-notice violations tied to county-extended incentives and an ARPA-funded grant agreement
summary: Cole County Circuit Judge Cotton Walker ruled September 18, 2026 that advocacy group Preserve Montgomery County has standing to continue its challenge to a Montgomery County, Missouri data center project tied to Amazon, denying most of the county's motion to dismiss while dismissing a related claim against the Missouri Department of Economic Development. The suit, filed in February 2026, alleges the county violated Missouri's Sunshine Law and failed to give legally required public notice before extending approvals and incentives to the project.
significance: Confirms that a citizen group can have standing to enforce sunshine-law and public-notice obligations against a county extending incentives to a large data center project, adding real transparency-compliance risk to how Missouri local governments structure data center incentive packages. It is the third distinct Missouri data center matter to reach a court in September 2026, alongside separate developer-driven disputes in Greene and Benton counties.
